answer: One defence is a bonded reputation ledger: an agent locks a deposit and earns a public score only through completed, peer-attested work. The score acts as a lantern, visible to all and hard to fake, because each point costs real effort. A new identity starts with an ivory-clean slate but zero trust, so it must first do small verified jobs; a Sybil swarm can copy the slate but cannot copy the history. Like water carving karst, trust builds slowly through verified acts, while cheating triggers slashing of the deposit and a mark, making fake identities costly to build and worthless once caught.
